source.title: LF-Steering: Latent Feature Activation Steering for Enhancing Semantic Consistency in Large Language Models
source.authors: Jingyuan Yang; Rong-Zhi Li; Wei-Xuan Wang; Ziyu Zhou; Zhi-Yong Feng; Wei Peng

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present. Some minor OCR or formatting artifacts appear, but they do not prevent reading the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies SAE-based feature identification and intervention to an LLM and reports results bearing on whether an SAE can recover useful sparse features in that setting. It does not reproduce the toy-model experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own SAE feature identifications and feature-level steering outcomes, which bear on V4. It does not test superposition geometry, capacity competition, or whether features are complete, stable canonical units. Results cited from earlier work are not recorded. Layer-location and hyperparameter sweeps are not rows because they are used to select settings; results for unrelated baseline steering methods and OOD locality are also omitted.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAE decomposition as a tool to steer LLama2-7B-Chat toward semantic consistency, and reports only its own method's task accuracy and consistency scores. It does not measure whether features are superposed, how many neurons features spread across, or how well the SAE recovers sparse features (no reconstruction, sparsity or interpretability rates). Two hand-picked feature interpretations (Table 2) are illustrative, not a measured recovery rate. The feature-level vs neuron-level comparison is a comparison of its own method variants on downstream accuracy.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that feature-level steering via a TopK SAE achieves state-of-the-art semantic consistency and task gains on NLU and NLG datasets. They say it is more precise, with lower interference, than component-level steering, citing its locality on out-of-domain datasets. They acknowledge that single-layer steering may be only a partial solution.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a TopK SAE on LLM activations, locates features associated with semantic inconsistency, and edits their activations during inference. It does not reproduce the toy-model setup or its geometric measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on feature-difference threshold and activation strength: the paper reports peak accuracy near threshold 0.10, declines at thresholds of 0.25 or higher, robustness across α values from 5.0 to 50.0, and degradation at α=50.0. These are described in the text, but the plotted values are not extracted as rows.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering SAE features (65,536-dim TopK SAE on one layer) improved downstream accuracy more than steering raw hidden states with the same method in LLama2-7B-Chat. Example: RobustBOOLQ 66.40 vs 50.50, baseline 46.40. The gain was small on RobustMRPC (68.38 vs 68.13).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interventions on SAE features are more effective for behaviour steering than interventions on raw hidden states.

fits_no_version.finding: Two manually inspected top-ranked SAE features were given readable interpretations: 'looking for answer' and 'location-related questions'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-relevant SAE features in chat LLMs admit human-readable interpretations (anecdotal).

record.problems: Evidence is limited to LLama2-7B-Chat and the selected layer and tasks. Selected feature interpretations are manually inspected examples. The study does not report a test of feature completeness, stability, or canonical status. Some reported outcome gains are small or mixed across measures.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. The feature-threshold and activation-strength sweeps in Figures 4 and 5 are mentioned in method_sensitivity but not extracted because their plotted values are not given in text. Layer-location accuracy in Figure 3 is used for layer selection rather than a result on the claim.

untested.parts: No toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
No measure of feature spread across neurons, or of SAE recovery quality (reconstruction, sparsity, interpretability rate). Only two illustrative features are shown.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: This is a steering-method paper that cites the polysemanticity issue (Elhage et al., 2022) as motivation and assumes SAE features are 'decoupled'. Rows r3–r7 duplicate r9, r11, r13, r15 and r17. None of the results measure superposition or SAE feature recovery, so no verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network feature-overlap geometry, sparsity transition, or regular geometric structure is measured.
The study does not test whether limited capacity causes important features to receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
No alternative cause of polysemantic neurons is tested.

The study tests SAE feature recovery and use in LLama2-7B-Chat, but not features spread across multiple neurons. It does not establish that the identified SAE features are exhaustive or that they generalize beyond the tested model, layer, and tasks.
The study does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable across settings, or canonical units of the model.
The study does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional structures.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Selected SAE features in LLama2-7B-Chat on RobustBOOLQ and PopQA Capital
reader_labels.reason: The authors identify and manually interpret SAE feature IDs, and feature-level steering reports improved accuracy on these tasks (r1, r2, r3, r7, r9, r17).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: PopQA Sport and RobustMRPC results, and the random-feature control
reader_labels.reason: Results are not uniformly positive across measures or conditions: PopQA Sport cosine similarity falls, RobustMRPC accuracy gains are modest, and random features perform worse than located features (r5, r6, r13, r15, r19).
